additional_concerns: Temporal alternatives remain unresolved: u3 states “With effect from 2 February 2026”, whereas u13 specifies launch at 9:00am and u28 says “following its implementation”. node.5d8c4ca625a46c41ff2f4098 includes pre-9:00am filings that the launch-based candidates exclude. The source supplies no explicit timezone. Neither interpretation should silently displace the other.

The blackout instruction in u12 permits direct contact for urgent submissions; it does not establish that every contact is an STR submission. Conversely, excluding the blackout from a post-launch rule does not establish that urgent reporting has no requirements.

node.a9c7e7d0e802f5a3fdf2abc2 treats certificate availability as sufficient under an acknowledged assumption. Footnote 3 states “Hongkong Post e-Cert (electronic certificate) is required for this submission.” It does not resolve possession, availability or required use mechanics. node.91c869d719c8872846f5adba delegates that unresolved assessment to ecert_requirement_satisfied.

Missing authority includes the separately supplied XML schema, prescribed PDF form, certificate-use instructions if needed to determine satisfaction, governing-timezone clarification, and promised resubmission guidance for performance details. The four opaque dependency IDs have no supplied mapping to these materials; no mapping can be inferred.

The selected channel, method and e-Cert control does not establish comprehensive XML compliance. Both executable compliance candidates explicitly leave schema conformity outside their XML-format facts.
node.27994712d6e50c0a1c05dea6 has no executable formalization. Its NOT_APPLICABLE finding for migrated-record access does not assess overall implementation completeness.

Resubmission candidates differ in their treatment of nonfiling events: node.29b224046d115582fbf223fb can return false, while the other event candidates place actual filing in scope and return OUT_OF_SCOPE. Preserve this distinction when defining the admissible event universe.

The history candidate asks whether a triggering event ever existed, not whether a resubmission duty remains outstanding. Later compliance must not erase a historical trigger. Its external aggregate still requires event linkage and adequate history evidence.
Conflict-anywhere blocking is an explicit runtime policy, not a requirement established by the circular. It can block evaluation even when a logically sufficient branch is known.
